To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new deep directed generative framework that is trained to match the energy-based probability estimator, which is a novel approach to training energy-based models that avoids the need for Markov chain sampling.

(1) a deep directed generativemodel can be trained to represent a given energy function; (2) the energy function can be used as a probability estimator; (3) the probability estimator can be trained to match the true distribution of a given dataset; and (4) a deep generative model can be trained to estimate the true distribution of data.

(1) we propose to train an energy function that represents the probability distribution, instead of a Markov chain that is derived from the energy function, and (2) we propose to use a generator network to approximate the sampling from the probability distribution.

we propose to train an energy-based generative model by minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the probability distribution estimated by a generator network and the energy function that the energy network is trained to approximate, and that the energy network can be used to estimate the probability of an input configuration by the exponential function of the energy value.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose to train an energy function and a generator in a way that they are mutually consistent and the generator is capable of generating samples from the distribution represented by the energy function.
, by combining energy-based models and deep generative models, we propose a framework for training a generative model whose samples can be obtained by running a single pass of the generator.

, by training a deep directed generativemodel with an energy-based probability estimator and a generative model that can be trained by backpropagation, we obtain a deep directed generatormodel that can be used to sample from the energy function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the energy function can be trained by minimizing a loss function that is based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the sampling distribution of the generator and the energy function, which is a tractable computation, and the generator can be trained to match the energy function in terms of the sampling distribution.

a generative model trained to match a given energy function can be viewed as a Markov chain Monte-Carlo sampler of that energy function, which can then be used for training of the energy function itself.
